subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: Should native exec approvals adopt the linked PR's additive deny-over-allow overlay, including human-only approval on matches and unioned rules across requested and host-local policy layers?
rationale: This changes an authorization boundary and persisted policy contract; code inspection cannot decide whether matched commands should prompt, hard-deny, or how independently configured gateway and node policy layers should compose.

options.title: Adopt deny-over-allow overlay
options.body: Keep existing security and ask modes, evaluate deny rules before permissive or durable allow decisions, and require explicit human approval for matches across both execution hosts.

options.title: Add a separate denylist mode
options.body: Implement the originally proposed security=denylist and ask=on-match enums as a distinct operating mode, accepting a larger configuration and migration surface.

options.title: Keep policy external
options.body: Decline native rules and rely on plugins such as CRE or external policy engines, accepting that core gateway/node approval parity may remain unavailable.

recommendation.title: Adopt deny-over-allow overlay
recommendation.body: Keep existing security and ask modes, evaluate deny rules before permissive or durable allow decisions, and require explicit human approval for matches across both execution hosts.

likelyOwner.reason: The exec-approval security model and recent major refactors route most strongly through this owner, who is also identified in repository governance as the project decision owner.
